articles.title: Jayden Daniels makes it clear how he feels about Dan Quinn
articles.summary: Jayden Daniels wants everyone to know how much he appreciates Dan Quinn.
articles.body:
Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels met with the media on Thursday and took full accountability for Sunday's end-of-game gaffe against the New York Giants that cost the team a win. Instead of improving to 2-3, Washington tied with the Giants and sits at 1-3-1 heading into Week 6.

"Just going back and reflecting on it and, you know, sitting back and ultimately, I know it's a lot of he say or whatever you're trying to make, but ultimately, like, it's on me at the end," Daniels said. "I know DQ is getting a lot of slack for it or whatever, you know, but regardless of what happens, I'm the person on the field that's supposed to calm everything, control everything, and I failed to the standard I told myself to and the standard in this organization. So, it's just something for me to move on. Not saying I'm proud of it or anything. Obviously, looking back, like, it could have resulted in a loss; we tied, but it was a fail in my eyes, and, you know, I know I'm better than that. I hold myself to a higher standard than that."

Daniels's statement was excellent and shows why he's considered such an outstanding leader. One part that stood out was his acknowledgment of what head coach Dan Quinn has gone through this week. Some in the media and among fans have called for Quinn's job, which is ridiculous. If you want to criticize Quinn for his record, that's understandable, but jumping on a soapbox to call for his job over Sunday's end-of-game debacle was foolish.

Daniels later explained what it meant to him that Quinn took the heat for Sunday's debacle.

"I mean, that's just the person he is, you know, the type of person that he is and obviously, you know, all eyes are on him, all eyes are on me," Daniels said. "And regardless of how people talk about him, we love DQ here. You know, I appreciate him. I always say that for making my dreams come true of being a starting quarterback in the NFL. And, you know, he helped me with the opportunity, so, super blessed to have DQ, and, you know, he means a lot to me."

If you had any doubt about how Washington's locker room will respond to Quinn, you shouldn't have any longer. Does that mean the Commanders will go out and upset the 49ers on Monday night? Of course not. But this team won't quit on Quinn. When he talks culture and character, that's what he's talking about. His team is built to respond to adversity and lean on one another in tough times.

Daniels and Quinn have maintained a close relationship since they both arrived in Washington in 2024. That relationship is closer than ever because of the difficult times they've faced together.

articles.title: Liverpool take giant step closer to Sergi Altimira
articles.summary: Liverpool are taking a step closer to signing Sergi Altimira or the next best thing. The Reds have shifted their plans.We've written this week that Liverpool...
articles.body:
Liverpool are taking a step closer to signing Sergi Altimira or the next best thing. The Reds have shifted their plans.

We've written this week that Liverpool are in the market for a new midfielder and that Sergi Altimira is on their radar. Anfield Watch and he might just be who they move for in 2027.

And that would be a fine move. Altimira is a really interesting player and one who our Value Adder model suggests held the highest defensive value per 90 minutes across the top five leagues last season.

Sporting certainly believed that. They moved to sign Altimira from Real Betis in the summer, replacing the outgoing Morten Hjulumnd, who signed for Atlético Madrid.

We think they've made an upgrade there - and it's drawn the attention of Liverpool. More than that, we think they're making true preparations to sign him.

Sergi Altimira is suddenly a perfect fit

We had real questions over the interest in Altimira. He is about as 'defensive midfielder' as it gets - tall, large turning circle, not particularly fast, and not one other consistently burst forward.

This flies in the face of everything Liverpool have produced in midfield for two years. The Reds have basically just used attacking midfielders, defiantly sticking with their philosophy even when they can't control a midfield and are losing game after game because of it.

Altimira's display against RC Lens this week, for instance, was the opposite. He sat at the base of a midfield three and spent large portions of the second half between split centre-backs. It's the Fabinho role at Liverpool - and one it appears they'd done away with.

However, Andoni Iraola is opening the door again. He's played with a sitting midfielder in each of his last two fixtures here, with Alexis Mac Allister doing it against Manchester City and Trey Nyoni against LASK.

Such a system means Altimira is a lot more likely to join as Liverpool suddenly do use a player in his role. And considering his numbers last season and this term, there aren't many better at it.

articles.title: Cruz Castillo's last-minute touchdown caps Brackenridge rally to beat Burbank
articles.summary: The running back rumbled into the end zone with 37 seconds left in the game to give the Eagles their first lead of the game and notch an important victory.
articles.body:
Joshua Garcia threw for two second-half scores and Cruz Castillo scored with 37 seconds remaining as Brackenridge rallied for a 21-14 win over Burbank on Thursday at SAISD Sports Complex.

Castillo's game-winning 28-yard touchdown run capped off a Brackenridge comeback in which the Eagles scored 21 unanswered points after falling behind 14-0 in the third quarter.

Brackenridge (5-2, 3-2) won its third game in a row, at least temporarily moving into sole possesion of fourth place in District 14-5A-II and putting itself in a position to earn its first playoff berth in five years. Brackenridge next meets Jefferson, which entered Week 8 tied with Eagles for the fourth playoff spot, next Friday at 7 p.m. at SAISD Sports Complex.

"We're a second-half team, and the kids know that," Brackenridge coach Steve Garcia said. "Our goal is to play good four quarters, and we haven't yet. At the most we've done is three great quarters, but we are a second-half team. The kids, they love the second half, and we always preach 0-0. It's literally 0-0 (at halftime), let's go out there and make some stops and we're going to win this ball game."

It didn't happen right away. After the slow, scoreless first half, Burbank (1-6, 1-4) took a 14-0 lead late in the third quarter thanks to a 34-yard touchdown run from Bryan Jalomo and a Christian Gutierrez 43-yard scoop-and-score.

But Castillo got it going for Brackenridge in the second half, as the senior running back finished with 141 yards on 28 carries. On his game-clinching touchdown, Castillo refused to go down, bouncing off a tackler before breaking to the outside to the end zone.

"I was just looking for the open lane, the linemen did a good job," Castillo said. "And I was like, 'You know what, let me just play physical' and that's what I did. I just bounced off one guy and I saw the open lane and I just went for it."

Joshua Garcia, the backup sophomore quarterback who has stepped in for the injured Ahmir Thompson, was in awe of Castillo's running style.

"Cruz is something else," Joshua Garcia said. "I've never seen anything like him, just a hard runner, dedicated, determined. He's just one of a kind." Brackenridge started its comeback with over two minutes left in the third quarter, when Joshua Garcia connected with Daniel Rincon on a 50-yard touchdown pass to cut the lead to 14-7.

Brackenridge defensive lineman Pedro Canizales Sanchez recovered a fumbled Burbank snap to set up the Eagles' next score, a 7-yard touchdown pass from Joshua Garcia to Damien Castro Diaz, who twisted to make a diving catch, tying the score at 14 with 6:45 left in the fourth quarter.

It was the second win a row for Brackenridge with Joshua Garcia at quarterback. After a rough start, Garcia finished with 108 yards on 10-of-18 passing, with an interception and two touchdowns.

"Definitely, getting more comfortable," Joshua Garcia said of having to step in the starting role. "Definitely doing what I'm told to do. Doing my job, getting comfortable back there and doing my thing."

Brackenridge won the turnover battle with two interceptions and a fumble recovery, while Burbank forced two turnovers, an interception and the Gutierrez fumble recovery that led to a score.

articles.title: EFI mess costs Indian riders global stage, FEI ban from Dec 1
articles.summary: New Delhi: Yet another tale of administrative chaos and athletes paying the price.
articles.body: New Delhi: Yet another tale of administrative chaos and athletes paying the price. Caught in a prolonged governance crisis at the Equestrian Federation of India (EFI), Indian riders now face a ban from international competitions, with their sporting futures hanging in the balance. The latest setback comes at a time when the govt is pushing to bring more international events to India and widen Indian athletes’ exposure to global competition.The International Equestrian Federation (FEI) has decided to suspend the EFI from Dec 1 over prolonged governance irregularities and failure to hold fresh elections, effectively shutting Indian riders, officials, trainers and horses out of international events. TOI is in possession of FEI’s Oct 15 letter confirming the decision, which was taken at the international body's board meeting on Oct 13.Explaining its move, the FEI said the EFI’s prolonged governance crisis had reached a tipping point. “The absence of elections to date to elect a new Executive Committee, has resulted in a prolonged governance and leadership irregularity that is no longer sustainable,” the letter by FEI Governance Director Francisco Lima stated.The crisis follows the Delhi high court’s dissolution of the EFI executive committee in Feb 2026. Its elected tenure had expired in Sept 2023, while fresh elections remain pending nine months after the court’s intervention. The Indian Olympic Association (IOA) constituted an ad hoc committee on March 27 to oversee the federation and facilitate the electoral process.While acknowledging the committee’s Sept 27 submission and its work, the FEI said elections were expected by Jan 31, 2027. However, the suspension will be reviewed only after the polls are held and evaluated by the international body.The consequences are sweeping. Citing its statutes, the FEI said the EFI “may not attend or be represented at any session or meeting of any FEI body, nor may it organise international events.” More damagingly, athletes, officials, trainers and horses “may not participate in international events organised by the FEI or any other national federation, whether under the Indian flag or the FEI flag.”With the suspension taking effect before the stated election deadline, Indian riders risk losing crucial international competition opportunities. articles.title: 'I questioned my coaches, challenged ideas': Indian shooting legend Abhinav Bindra urges athletes to 'question' more
articles.summary: Indian shooting legend Abhinav Bindra on Friday stressed that athletes should be free to question their training methods, coaches and the system around
articles.body: Indian shooting legend Abhinav Bindra on Friday stressed that athletes should be free to question their training methods, coaches and the system around them to improve their performance. He said asking questions should not be seen as a lack of discipline, as it helps athletes learn and grow.The 44-year-old shared his thoughts on X but did not mention what prompted his remarks. Bindra, who won India's first individual Olympic gold medal in 2008, said his curiosity and habit of questioning things played a key role in his success."Throughout my sporting career, I questioned my coaches, challenged ideas and remained curious. Not because I lacked respect but because I wanted to understand, learn and get better," he posted.He also warned that athletes who are unable to express themselves freely may eventually stop questioning things altogether, which could hurt their growth and sporting success.Questioning can help athletes improveBindra said athletes should be encouraged to examine their own performances, question their coaches and understand the methods they are asked to follow. He believes this should come from a desire to improve rather than an intention to challenge authority."We need athletes who question their own work, their coaches, the methods recommended to them and the structures they operate within. Not out of defiance but out of a genuine desire to improve," he explained.He added that what some people see as "indiscipline" may actually be necessary for an athlete's development. According to Bindra, there is a clear difference between refusing to learn and continuing to ask questions to gain a better understanding of the sport."What some might consider indiscipline may, in fact, be essential to growth. There is a difference between an athlete who refuses to learn and one who refuses to stop asking questions. Sport must be wise enough to recognise that difference," added the 44-year-old.A career beyond Olympic gloryBindra is considered one of India's greatest sportspersons. Along with his historic Olympic gold medal, he has also won gold at the World Championships.After retiring from competitive shooting, he served as vice-chair of the International Olympic Committee's Athletes' Commission for eight years, completing his term earlier this year.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India vs West Indies: Fifth T20 International – teams, start, lineups, Hope
articles.summary: India host West Indies in the final match of the tour on Saturday with an all-time classic T20 series level at 2-2.
articles.body:
Who: India vs West Indies What: Twenty20 International cricket series Where: M Chinnaswamy Stadium, Bengaluru, India When: Saturday, October 17, at 7pm (13:30 GMT) How to follow: Al Jazeera Sport will have all the build-up from 11:30 GMT before our live text commentary stream

India host West Indies in the decisive T20 International series finale on Saturday after one of the most compelling white-ball tours in recent memory.

The five-game series is level at 2-2 before the match in Bengaluru after record-breaking feats by the tourists that have pushed the T20 World Cup holders to the limit.

Al Jazeera Sport takes a look at what has become a must-not-miss showdown.

How did West Indies tour of India begin?

The teams played a three-match One-Day International to begin the white-ball tour, which saw India take an unassailable lead after opening eight-wicket wins in Thiruvananthapuram and Guwahati.

After posting a mammoth 351-7 off their 50 overs – thanks largely to KL Rahul’s 129 off 87 balls – in New Chandigarh, India would have felt they had enough on the board to claim the third match, too.

Enter West Indies captain Shai Hope. The opener hit 162 off 143 balls in an unbeaten knock that led his side to a five-wicket win .

It was the West Indies highest ODI run chase.

How did the India-West Indies T20 series begin?

India put the disappointment of the closing defeat in the ODI series behind them by claiming an eight-win win, with 5.2 overs to spare, in the first T20 of the series.

Despite fifties from Hope and Sherfane Rutherford, West Indies were bowled out for 171, with Naman Dhir taking three wickets for the hosts.

Hope then hit an unbeaten 102 off only 45 balls in the second match to lead West Indies to their highest successful Twenty20 run chase .

Hope hit nine sixes and six boundaries as the West Indies finished with 252-4 in reply to India’s 249-5.

India restored their series lead in the third match, but only via a narrow 14-run victory.

After being bowled out off the last ball of their innings, India posted 223 – led by Abhishek Sharma’s 69 off 30 balls.

Arshdeep Singh claimed three wickets as West Indies were restricted to 209-7.

What happened in the last India-West Indies T20?

It was time for the Hope show again in the fourth game of the T20 tour, as the wicketkeeper-batter hit his second century of the series .

The tourists struck 247-3, having been put in, with Hope hitting an unbeaten 102.

His nine sixes and four fours were a record tally for a West Indies batter in a T20 International.

The total was the second-highest first innings score in T20s against India, trailing England’s 257-3 in Southampton this year.

Opener Sanju Samson’s 56 off 23 balls set India off to a good start, but Keemo Paul’s five-wicket haul led West Indies to a 24-run series levelling win.

What did Shai Hope joke about his Player of the Match awards?

Hope joked after the fourth T20 that he was worried he may ⁠have to fork ⁠out excess baggage fees after picking up his third Player of the Match award on their tour of India.

“To be honest, they are a bit heavy, and we have got to look at the luggage weight,” he quipped after the win.

“I think we are going to have some problems going back home.”

articles.summary: The Street Fighter franchise is loaded with iconic characters, and a live-action version of the classic game needs a cast that can bring its fighters to life.
articles.body:
The Street Fighter franchise is loaded with iconic characters, and a live-action version of the classic game needs a cast that can bring its fighters to life.

WWE has no shortage of larger-than-life personalities who could fit right into the Street Fighter universe, from dominant champions to unpredictable villains.

With Roman Reigns retaining his movie role as Akuma and Cody Rhodes remaining as Guile, here is how Hollywood could cast other iconic Street Fighter characters using WWE Superstars.

Predicting Survivor Series Participants 🔮

WWE Moments That Could Be Horror Movies 😱

M. Bison is one of the most feared villains in Street Fighter, and Lesnar has the legitimate fighting background and intimidating presence to make the criminal mastermind a terrifying opponent.

The Beast Incarnate looks like someone who could take over the world by force, making him an ideal choice to lead the game's villainous organization.

Gunther's methodical, hard-hitting style makes him a natural fit for Sagat, the towering muay thai master known for his devastating strikes.

Both are imposing competitors who can overwhelm opponents without relying on flashy theatrics, and Gunther would bring the physical credibility needed to portray one of Ryu's most dangerous rivals.

Blanka is an unpredictable fighter whose wild movements and explosive aggression set him apart from the rest of the roster.

Fatu possesses that same chaotic energy, combining athleticism with an aggressive style that could make his version of the Brazilian brawler a memorable addition to the cast.

Zangief is a powerhouse who relies on brute strength and devastating wrestling moves, making Femi an obvious choice for the Russian grappler.

Femi's size, strength and dominant presence would translate perfectly to a character who can turn a fight around with a single throw.

Chun-Li is one of gaming's most recognizable female fighters, combining extraordinary athleticism with technical striking ability.

Belair's strength, speed and confidence make her an excellent fit for the Interpol agent, while her natural charisma would help bring the iconic character to life beyond the fight scenes.

Ryu is one of the most iconic characters in fighting game history, known for his discipline, determination, and relentless drive to improve as a fighter. Orton’s veteran presence, calculated in-ring style, and ability to strike without warning make him a fitting choice for the martial arts master.

The Viper has spent decades establishing himself as one of WWE’s most dangerous competitors, and that experience would translate well to Ryu’s composed approach to combat.

Vega is a vain, agile fighter who combines acrobatic movement with a distinctive masked appearance.

Bálor has the athleticism and theatrical instincts to capture that combination, especially when drawing on the darker presentation of his Demon persona.

Ken Masters is Ryu's brash, confident rival, bringing plenty of personality to the franchise's central fighting duo.

LA Knight has the swagger, charisma and self-assurance to make the role work, delivering a version of Masters who can match Ryu in the ring and steal the spotlight outside it.

Juri Han is unpredictable, sadistic and dangerous, with a playful personality that often masks her cruel intentions.

Asuka's ability to shift between eccentric humor and frightening intensity makes her an ideal choice, while her striking background would help sell Juri's fast, unconventional fighting style.

Dhalsim is a mystical yoga master whose unusual fighting style and flexible movements separate him from the rest of the Street Fighter roster.

Nakamura's distinctive movement, striking ability and eccentric presentation could make for an entertaining character, especially if the adaptation embraces Dhalsim's stranger qualities.

E. Honda is a proud sumo wrestler who combines tremendous strength with surprising speed and agility.

Otis has the size, power and comedic timing to capture the character's larger-than-life personality, while his wrestling background would make Honda's sumo-inspired attacks a natural fit.

articles.title: 5 NHL Trade Landing Spots for Jake DeBrusk Amid NHL Rumors
articles.summary: We are just over two weeks into the 2026-27 NHL season, and the trade deadline is still several months away, but it is not too early to at least have some idea as to who some of the sellers will be.
articles.body:
We are just over two weeks into the 2026-27 NHL season, and the trade deadline is still several months away, but it is not too early to at least have some idea as to who some of the sellers will be.

The Vancouver Canucks, a team in the very early stages of an extensive rebuild, are likely to be one of them, and forward Jake DeBrusk is likely to be one of the potential trade chips they have.

He already hinted at not wanting to be a part of a long-term rebuild during the 2025-26 season (before later attempting to clarify those remarks), and is the type of player who probably doesn't fit in with where the Canucks are going in the short term.

DeBrusk turns 30 this weekend and is probably one of the veteran players still on the Canucks roster who might have some trade value. He also has a full no-movement clause through this season, so he would have to approve any trade.

The fact that he is about to become 30 and still has four full years remaining on his contract after this one is a bit of a concern, but his salary-cap number is going to turn into less of a concern in the coming seasons as the cap continues to rise.

A $5.5 million cap hit for a potential 20-goal, 45-point forward is going to start looking like a bargain—assuming he continues to score and play at that level.

So with all of that said, let's take a look at five teams around the league that could (or perhaps should) have some interest in potentially acquiring him at some point this season.

After taking a huge step forward in their rebuild in 2025-26 and reaching the Eastern Conference Final, there are big expectations this season for the Montreal Canadiens. There is a good reason for it.

With Nick Suzuki, Cole Caufield, Juraj Slafkovsky, Ivan Demidov, Lane Hutson and Noah Dobson they have one of the NHL's best young cores, with all of them locked into long-term deals that should age gracefully and continue to be team-friendly deals for the long term.

While they are very good with a great future, they are still not a finished product. They still need some help in the lower half of their lineup, and after a quiet offseason that only saw them add Chris Kreider, that is still the case.

DeBrusk wouldn't need to be a major play-driver here and could easily settle into a middle-six role on the left side and chip in some much-needed secondary scoring, both now and in the short term future.

The Oilers are off to a fantastic start in the standings, but the gap between their top players and second- and third-tier players is still huge.

When Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl are on the ice together? They are outscoring teams 11-1 during 5-on-5 play.

When only one is on the ice? Outscoring teams by a 4-2 margin.

When neither is on the ice? Getting outscored 5-9 with truly awful underlying and scoring chance numbers.

This recipe has not worked for almost 10 years now when it comes to winning a championship, and it is not going to work this season, even if it results in a better regular-season record.

They still have a lot of holes, and a lot of spots that need to be plugged. Goalie is one of them. Defensive depth is another. And so is scoring depth at forward. Their second, third and fourth lines are just not up to par for a championship team, and it has to be addressed at some point over the next few months.

A player like DeBrusk—or any player who can provide some secondary scoring—should be on their radar.

Just because the Senators traded Brady Tkachuk over the summer does not mean they are throwing in the towel on this season and not trying to win.

They should still have reason to believe they can be a playoff team in the Eastern Conference, and with a 6-2-0 start through their first eight games, they are making a strong case for it.

That said, they could still use a little more offense in the middle of their lineup, especially after losing William Eklund, one of their big offseason additions, to a major injury that is going to keep him out for several months.

Moving Tkachuk not only eliminated the distraction that came with their captain not wanting to be there and waiting for his chance to leave, it also opened up a little extra salary-cap space that they could use to add more pieces.

DeBrusk wouldn't be a huge difference-maker, but he would be a nice addition to help add a little more scoring punch to a team that does need to replace a lot of goal-scoring.

The Los Angeles Kings are off to a miserable start, but this doesn't strike me as a team that is going to be quick to throw in the towel this season.

They have been a playoff team five years in a row (with five first-round exits), and no doubt expect to be there again despite winning zero of their first five games.

Do they have a high ceiling? Probably not. Are they going to be a serious contender? Not likely. But the Pacific Division should still be wide open for them to have a shot to play their way back into the race. If they are going to get there, and if they are going to have any chance of making some noise, finding additional offense is going to have to be a big priority.

DeBrusk wouldn't likely be enough to move the needle a lot, but it's really hard to see where the offense is going to come from with this roster as currently constructed.

Artemi Panarin and Kevin Fiala are good wingers, and Quinton Byfield still has the upside and the hope of being a top-line player, but there is a significant drop-off after that. Keep in mind, only four players scored more than 15 goals on this team a year ago, while they ranked 29th in goals scored as a team.

And the offseason did not provide enough to make that change.

They still need to be in the market for a lot more offense.

The Minnesota Wild need to be all-in this season given the uncertainty surrounding the future of superstar defenseman Quinn Hughes and whether he wants to re-sign.

So why not reunite him with one of his former Vancouver teammates who could also help fill a big need?

While center depth is the more pressing requirement for the Wild, that doesn't mean they don't still have a need for additional scoring depth on the wings.

Kirill Kaprizov and Hughes (along with the goaltending) are the big difference-makers here, and they can take the Wild far during the regular season and playoffs, but the lineup does need some more work around the edges to really make them a serious Stanley Cup contender.

articles.title: Stats and Snaps – NFL Week 5: Giants @ Commanders
articles.summary: The Commanders find creative ways to avoid winning
articles.body:
I count myself among the more optimistic Washington Football fans since Josh Harris took over ownership from the Shrek villain. Nevertheless, last Sunday's failure to beat the Giants strained my ability to keep a positive outlook, even more than the previous week's loss to the Colts.

The reason for that was the team's sheer determination to avoid winning, despite multiple advantages working in their favor and opportunities left on the field.

The failure of clock management in the final series of the game has been discussed at length, so there is no need to re-litigate that here. However, even prior to the Commanders possessing the ball on the Giants' 24 yd line, with 12 sec remaining in overtime, the franchise was working hard to find ways to deny itself the victory.

In the two games prior to Sunday's embarrassing 27-27 overtime tie with the Giants, the Commanders' run blocking collapsed, leaving them unable to establish a running game with lead back Bill Croskey-Merritt. Against the Giants, the run blocking was much improved – not just due to the return of Sam Cosmi to the line-up, but across the board. In the first half, Bill rushed for 51 yds and a TD, averaging 7.3 Y/A. For some reason, the Commanders turned away from the run in the second half and overtime, giving Bill just 4 touches in 3 quarters of football, and none in overtime – even as he increased his average 7.8 Y/A in the second half.

The mid-game adjustments on defense mirrored those on offense. Warren Sharp of Sharp Analytics has pointed out how the Commanders switched coverage from a scheme which was working in the first half, and allowed Jameis Winston to lead a comeback:

For what seems like an eternity, Washington fans have been wishing for a coaching staff with the ability to make adjustments when game plans aren't working. Against the Giants, they inexplicably adjusted game plans which were working, with predictable results. It was the type of effort which gets coaches fired.

The tie gave the Commanders sole possession of last place in the division, with a 1-3-1 record. Head coach Dan Quinn is running out of opportunities to turn the season around. Hopefully, he and his coaching staff have learned the lessons which can be drawn from the disappointing tie, which should have been a win.

Despite the result, there were some flashes of promise which the team might be able to build on against the 49ers, including standout performances by Jayden Daniels (up to the last play), Bill Croskey-Merritt, Sam Cosmi, K'Lavon Chaisson, Daron Payne, Sonny Styles and Amik Robertson and great plays from many of their teammates.

With key players like Nick Cross and Trey Amos potentially returning from injury, the heat under Quinn's seat might provide the motivation he needs to lift his game and take the fight to the heavily favored 49ers.

But before we get ahead of ourselves, let's take a final look at who played where, who stood out, and who showed areas for improvement in the Commanders' tie with the New York Giants.

Stats & Snaps Going on Hiatus: The Stats and Snaps will be taking a two week holiday, and will return after the Eagles game on November 1. In its place, I will be doing a 1/3 season stats roundup of the Commanders' players during the week before the Eagles game.

These plays had the largest impact on teams' scoring potential within a drive, as judged by Expected Points Added (EPA). Threshhold: EPA = +/- 2.25

Q3, 7:56, 2 nd and 6 at NYG 38: Jayden Daniels scrambles up the middle for 38 yards, touchdown. EPA 4.22

Q4, 11:13, 3 rd and 2 at NYG 26: Jayden Daniels scrambles left tackle for 26 yards, touchdown. EPA 3.86

Q1, 13:07, 1 st and 10 at NYG 33: Jacory Croskey-Merritt up the middle for 33 yards, touchdown. EPA 3.62

Q2, 0:07, 4 th and 10 at WAS 39: Dominic Zvada 57 yard field goal no good. EPA -2.72

Q1, 7:15, 4 th and 12 at WAS 32: Dominic Zvada 50 yard field goal no good. EPA -2.84

OT, 8:01, 4 th and 8 at WAS 28: Dominic Zvada 46 yard field goal no good. EPA -2.92

OT, 2:00, 1 st and 10 at WAS 24: Cam Skattebo up the middle for no gain. Cam Skattebo fumbles, recovered by Shy Tuttle at WAS-24 (tackle by Sonny Styles). EPA -4.45

Q2, 2:09, 2 nd and 8 at NYG 47: Jameis Winston sacked by K'Lavon Chaisson for 8 yards. Jameis Winston fumbles (forced by K'Lavon Chaisson), recovered by Tim Settle at NYG-28 and returned for 1 yard. EPA -5.43

Q4, 7:24, 4 th and 8 at WAS 17: Jameis Winston pass complete short middle to Isaiah Likely for 17 yards, touchdown. EPA 4.69

Q3, 5:35, 4 th and 4 at WAS 43: Jameis Winston pass complete short right to Tyrone Tracy for 21 yards. EPA 3.71

Q3, 1:47, 3 rd and 9 at WAS 10: Jameis Winston pass short middle is intercepted by Amik Robertson at WAS-1 and returned for no gain. Penalty on Amik Robertson: Defensive Pass Interference, 9 yards. EPA 3.67

Q4, 1:48, 1 st and 10 at WAS 17: Jameis Winston pass complete deep middle to Malik Nabers for 17 yards, touchdown. EPA 2.56

Q1, 10:23, 3 rd and 13 at NYG 40: Jameis Winston pass complete short left to Isaiah Likely for 15 yards. EPA 2:42

Q3, 0:47, 3 rd and 3 at WAS 3: Jameis Winston pass complete short right to Isaiah Likely for 3 yards, touchdown. EPA 2.28

OT, 0:15, 2 nd and 8 at NYG 24: Jayden Daniels sacked by Tremaine Edmunds for no gain. EPA -3.57

A big question on Jayden Daniels ' return from injury was whether he would be able to run with a brace on his left arm. The Commanders' star QB answered that one by leading the team in rushing, with an impressive 103 yds, 2 TDs and 4 first downs in 9 attempts (11.4 Y/A; 55.6% success rate). His rushing total was the 7 th highest in Week 5 at any position, and he was one of three players with over 100 rushing yds and 2 rushing TDs.

JD5 was also effective in the air, completing 17/25 attempts (68%, ADOT 8.2 yds) for 199 yds, 0 INT and 0 TD (40% success rate). He was sacked 5 times for 23 yds and faced 15 total pressures (40.5% of dropbacks), per PFF, but did a good job of protecting the ball and avoiding turnovers.

His mental lapse on the last play of overtime did negate an opportunity to go for a game winning field goal. But that is not recorded on the stat sheet.

Daniels was also penalized 5 yards for delay of game in overtime.

Aside from those mistakes, Daniels had an excellent game. His 80.9 total QBR ranked 5 th best among starting QBs in Week 5.

Advanced rushing stats (YBC, broken tackles) were sourced from PFR

Jacory Croskey-Merritt was curiously second in playing time, despite being by far the most effective running back in the game. Bill bounced back from a string of unimpressive performances to post his best game of the season, toting the rock 11 times for 82 yds (7.45 Y/A), 1 TD and 4 first downs, with 1 broken tackle. His 63.6% rushing success rate was the 5 th highest among NFL players in Week 5 (min 10 attempts).

Bill got most of his action in the first half (7 att, 51 yds, 1 TD), got light duty in the second half (4 att, 31 yds), and did not get a touch in overtime.

Bill's rebound most likely had a lot to do with a big improvement in run blocking, as measured by PFF grades (see OL, below). Consistent with that take, he averaged a whopping 5.3 yards before contact/attempt this week, up from 0.4 YBC/att against the Colts and 1.0 YBC/att against the Seahawks.

Rachaad White had 9 carries for 18 yds and no first downs (2.57 Y/A, 42.9% success rate), while averaging just 1 YBC/att. He caught his lone target as a receiver for 2 yds.

White was penalized 5 yds for a false start in the 2 nd quarter. It was just the second penalty of his career.

A week after averaging 7.25 Y/A on 4 carries against the Colts, Austin Ekeler plummeted to 3 attempts for -1 yd, and -0.3 YBC/att. He caught his only passing target for 15 yds.

Advanced receiving stats were sourced from PFF.

Making an early return from a hamstring injury, Terry McLaurin led the team in receiving yards, catching 4/4 targets for 62 yds (100% rec, ADOT 9.8 yds). As we have come to expect, he was 2/2 on contested targets. Terry was the Commanders' third-most productive receiver, at an impressive 2.21 Y/RR.

Antonio Williams played predominantly in the slot this week, marking a departure from previous weeks, when he split time more evenly between the slot and wide out. Williams caught 3/3 targets for 31 yds (ADOT 7.0 yds), and had modest productivity (1.11 Y/RR).

Treylon Burks caught 2/5 targets for 26 yds (40% rec, ADOT 9.0 yds). His productivity was on the low side (0.96 Y/RR). On a more positive note, Burks posted the highest run blocking grade on the team (76.6).

Dyami Brown caught 1/2 targets for 2 yds. Van Jefferson was not targeted on 1 receiving route.

Chig Okonkwo 's return to the lineup brought some visibility back to the TE group, which seemed to have gone missing for the past few weeks. Chig was close behind Terry with 60 receiving yards on 4 receptions and 6 targets. He was the Commanders' second-most productive receiver at 2.40 Y/RR, and led the team with 34 yards after the catch. He was second on the team in average YAC, at an impressive 8.5 YAC/rec, but well behind Austin Ekeler at 13.0 YAC/rec.

John Bates caught his lone target for 1 yard. He was also penalized 5 yds for a false start in the 2 nd quarter.

If PFF run blocking grades are to be believed, Ben Sinnott had his best game of the season as a lead blocker. His 72.1 run blocking grade was the 4 th highest on the team, and well above his 52.3 season average.

Pressure counts and run blocking grades were sourced from PFF.

This is the first game of the season when all five offensive linemen have played 100% of snaps at their primary positions.

LT Brandon Coleman had a rough afternoon against EDs Kayvon Thibodeaux and Abdul Carter. He allowed 2 sacks and 2 QB hurries in 37 pressure opportunities. Coleman's 10.8% pressure rate allowed is about twice what you would hope to see from a starting OT. On the bright side, his 73.8 run blocking grade was third-highest on the team, and represented a major recovery from the lowest grade of his career posted last week against the Colts.

Coleman committed a false start (5 yds) in the 2 nd quarter, as well as a holding call, which was declined.

LG Chris Paul allowed just 1 QB hurry in pass protection (2.7% pressure rate), which was consistent with his play this season. His 58.5 run blocking grade is a little below average for starting guards, but was his highest grade this season and a massive improvement over the second-lowest grade of his career posted last week.

C Lucas Patrick once again allowed 0 pressures in pass protection. That is not unusual for Patrick. According to PFF, he is riding the 3 rd longest active streaks without allowing a sack among NFL linemen. He has not allowed a sack in 1,031 pass blocking snaps, dating back to 2022. Patrick had a down week in run blocking. His 54.7 run blocking grade was a big drop from 73.0 against the Colts.

Sam Cosmi 's return to the lineup was a massive upgrade to the RG position over Matt Gulbin and Nick Allegretti. Cosmi allowed no pressures in protection. His 74.4 run blocking grade was the highest on the OL, and the 13 th highest among 73 guards in Week 5.

Like his bookend, Josh Conerly struggled at times against the Giants edge rushers. Like Coleman, he allowed 4 pressures (10.8% pressure rate). But unlike his teammate, Conerly did not allow any sacks or QB hits, only hurries. Conerly has graded well in run blocking consistently this season, with the lone exception of the Colts game last week. His 65.4 run blocking grade against the Giants was a little below his season average, but was a big improvement over his season low mark (44.6) in London.

Pressure stats were sourced from PFF and NFL official stats.

K'lavon Chaisson made 1 TFL, 1 sack, 2 QB hits, 3 QB hurries, and 1 forced fumble. His 17.6% pressure rate in the pass rush was above the 90 th percentile for edge rushers based on 2025 stats. His strip sack of Jameis Winston for a turnover in the 2 nd quarter was the biggest play of the game for either team, as judged by EPA (-5.43).

K'Lavon dropped into coverage 6 times (15% of pass plays), but there was disagreement on his coverage stats (PFF: 2/2, 20 yds; PFR: 1/1, 6 yds).

Dorance Armstrong made 1 tackle and 2 assists. In the pass rush, he registered 2 QB hits and 2 hurries (pressure rate 10.8%). He drew a 15 yd personal foul for a facemask in the first quarter.

Joshua Josephs made 1 tackle for a stop on a pass play. He dropped into coverage 6 times (40%) and was not targeted.

Odafe Oweh registered 1 QB hurry, per PFF. He drew a 15 yard personal foul for a facemask in overtime.

Daron Payne took over half of his defensive snaps at DE. He made 1 TFL, 2 assists and 1 FF. In the pass rush, he registered 1 sack for 13 yds and 2 QB hurries. His 6.5% pressure rate is a little below average for iDL.

In his first game back from injury, Deatrich Wise made 3 tackles, 2 of which were run stops. His 18.2% run stop rate is an elite figure for an iDL.

Javon Kinlaw made 2 tackle assists, contributing to 1 stop, and registered 1 QB hit.

Shy Tuttle made 2 tackle assists, contributing to 2 stops, and recovered the Cam Skattebo fumble in overtime. He generated 1 QB hurry in the pass rush.

Tim Settle made 1 tackle assist on a stop. He also recovered the fumble on K'Lavon Chaisson's strip sack.

Sonny Styles led the Commanders in combined tackles, with 4 tackles and 9 assists, including 1 TFL and 2 total stops. He generated 1 QB hurry in 12 blitzes. PFR counted 2 missed tackles, while PFF counted 3.

There was some disagreement on his coverage stats, which PFF recording 4 rec/4 tgt for 49 yds (0.92 Y/Cov Snp – not bad) and PFR recording 4 rec/5 tgt for 33 yds (0.62 Y/Cov Snp – great) and 1 TD. The NFL recorded 1 PD.

Frankie Luvu made 6 tackles and 3 assists, including 4 stops. His 12.5% run stop rate was above the 90 th percentile for LBs. He registered 1 QB hit and 1 hurry in 13 blitzes.

Luvu's coverage stats were wildly different between PFR (0.13 Y/Cov Snp – outstanding) and PFF (0.83 Y/Cov Snp – good).

The official snap counts show Kain Medrano on the field for 1 defensive play. But PFF did not see him, so it's unclear where he lined up. He did not appear on the stat sheet.

Rasul Douglas made 9 tackles and 1 assist, including 2 TFL.

There was some disagreement on his coverage performance, with PFR rating him as outstanding (4 rec/9 tgt, 39 yds, 0.63 Y/Cov Snp), while PFF saw him as a little more hit and miss (5 rec/9 tgt, 55 yds, 1 TD, 0.89 Y/Cov Snp). The official stats recorded 1 PD.

Rasul collected a 5 yd holding penalty in the 2 nd quarter.

Amik Robertson recorded 6 tackles, 1 assist, 2 run stops and 1 PD. Amik's 8.7% run stop rate is an elite figure for CBs. Through 5 games, Amik ranks 4 th among NFL CBs in total stops (12, tie with Kamari Lassiter) and 4 th in run stop rate (3.8%, min 100 run def. snaps).

There was significant disagreement over his coverage, with PFF rating him in the lockdown range (0.58 Y/Cov Snp) and PFR rating him about average (1.03 Y/Cov Snp).

Amik drew a questionable DPI penalty for 9 yds, negating an INT in the 3 rd quarter. He was also penalized 5 yds for holding in the 4 th quarter.

Mike Sainristil was back in action this week, playing predominantly in the slot. He recorded 2 tackles and 1 assist, with 1 stop.

There was consensus that he had another bad day in coverage, allowing 3 rec/5 tgt for 49 yds (1.58 Y/Cov Snp – below 10 th percentile) and 1 TD.

Fabian Moreau made 4 tackles, 2 stops and 1 PD in just 26 defensive snaps.

He was fairly leaky in coverage, allowing 4 rec/5 tgts for 33 yds in 24 coverage snaps (1.37 Y/Cov Snp – between 10 th and 25 th percentile).

Quan Martin made 3 tackles and 5 assists, with 1 stop.

While there was slight disagreement over the details, his coverage figures were pretty good (PFF 24 yds, 1 TD, 0.39 Y/Cov Snp; PFR 14 yds, 0.23 Y/Cov Snp).

Jeremy Reaves made 3 tackles, 2 assists, with 1 stop and 1 PD. PFR counted 1 missed tackle and PFF counted 2. He generated 3 pressures in 11 blitzes (27.3% pressure rate).

There was moderate disagreement over his coverage performance, with PFF rating him in the outstanding range in 52 coverage snaps (3 rec/6 tgt, 9 yds, 0.17 Y/Cov Snp) and PFR rating him as very good (3 rec/6 tgt, 33 yds, 0.63 Y/Cov Snp).

Drew Stevens was 2/2 on field goals from 28 and 40 yds. He was 1/2 on extra points. Through 5 games, he is 8/11 on extra points and 9/11 on field goals.

Rachaad White returned 4 kickoffs for 100 yds (25 Y/A) with a long of 32.

Luke McCaffrey returned 2 kickoffs for 41 yds.

Antonio Williams returned 1 punt for 2 yds and made 1 fair catch.

Colson Yankoff led the coverage units with 3 tackles.

Mike Sainristil and Javontae Jean-Baptiste had 2 tackles apiece.

Austin Keys made 1 tackle and 2 assists.

Luke McCaffrey made 1 tackle, 1 assist and 1 missed tackle.

Darren Hall and Isaac Yiadom made 1 tackle apiece.

There were no penalties on special teams this week.

articles.title: Missing out on recruits is not a sign trouble
articles.summary: Tommy Lloyd can’t recruit American players. At least, so was the fear until he started landing some of the best the country had to offer, including Caleb Hol...
articles.body:
Tommy Lloyd can't recruit American players.

At least, so was the fear until he started landing some of the best the country had to offer, including Caleb Holt , Cameron Holmes , Koa Peat , Brayden Burries and Carter Bryant .

Tommy Lloyd can't pull elite talent from the transfer portal.

Pelle Larsson and Oumar Ballo would like a word, as would Caleb Love , Keshad Johnson , Jaden Bradley , Tobe Awaka and Anthony Dell'Orso . Derek Dixon and JJ Mandaquit , too.

Tommy Lloyd can't get Arizona to the Final Four.

At least, that was the concern until he did exactly that.

Ever since Lloyd was hired as Arizona's head coach in April 2021 there have been doubters. Understanding that there are fewer now than there were five years ago, the coach is not immune to criticism, critique or worry.

The latest chatter surrounded he and Arizona's "missing" of recruits Darius Wabbington and Kamsi Awaka . A pair of bigs from the 2027 class, the former chose Indiana over the top school in his home state and the latter decided on Florida rather than the coach and school who propelled his older brother to the NBA.

No doubt seeing them commit elsewhere stung. Lloyd and the Wildcats wanted each of them for a reason, and to lose out on both in consecutive days was jarring to many who cheer for Arizona. To some, it was a sign that Lloyd's style of recruiting was an issue and that the program could be in some trouble.

It's a good thing the transfer portal exists.

Now, it's true this previous offseason wasn't as flashy as many of us thought it would be following a trip to the Final Four. It was assumed recent success would lead to a recruiting windfall, with players falling over themselves to play their home games at the McKale Center. That hasn't exactly been the case, and to some missing out on recruiting targets gives the appearance of a program that may not have what it takes to continue to compete at the highest level.

Then again, that Arizona is coming off a Final Four and currently finds itself at or near the top of various rankings, be it Big 12 power , KenPom , EvanMiya or most everywhere else. The Cats were just recently picked to win the Big 12 , while three players — Mo Krivas, Ivan Kharchenkov and Holt were named to one of the preseason all-conference teams. Krivas was also named Big 12 Preseason Player of the Year.

Arizona was really good last season. Arizona is expected to be really good this season.

Under Lloyd Arizona has been one of the best teams in the country every season, with the Cats earning two No. 1 seeds, two No. 2 seeds and a No. 4 seed in the NCAA Tournament. Conference titles have also been part of the journey, along with numerous ranked victories.

So tell me again why people are down on Arizona because it didn't get commitments from a couple of high school kids that have nothing to do with the season that still hasn't officially started?

Perhaps that's just an Arizona fan's natural state, being nervous when life is going well and going into a full-blown panic when something doesn't go according to plan.

The Arizona Basketball brand is in a good place these days. The Final Four drought is in the past, and with it is the pressure that had to be felt, at least a little, by Lloyd. It was certainly a weight on Sean Miller's shoulders.

Fans felt it, too. Evidently many still feel it, insomuch as they are constantly waiting for the rug to be pulled out from under them or for that other shoe to drop.

Tommy Lloyd has proven himself to be one of the best coaches in the country. You can quibble with any part of his process, though he would probably tell you there is still plenty he can get better at.

Maybe he should allocate whatever financial resources he has differently. Offering more players scholarships rather than focusing on a select handful of players could be an option, too.

But whatever issues you may have with Lloyd the recruiter, or even Lloyd the coach, there are few schools in the country who wouldn't love to have him lead their program. Arizona landed a gem in the wake of Miller's dismissal, finding a coach who was able to not just rebuild the program in the aftermath of its off-court issues but make it even stronger than before. There's a reason North Carolina so heavily pursued Lloyd, and a reason why we all breathed a sigh of relief when he chose to remain in Tucson and will always worry, at least a little, that a different blue blood might be more successful in convincing him to leave.

Until such a time comes, though, Arizona has one of the best coaches in the country. And while he's not infallible or perfect, Lloyd has provided every reason to believe that when the 2027 Wildcats take the floor talent will not be an issue.

There were a lot of comments at some point in the past eleven months or so that said something like, "Who cares about xyz, you'll do it for a chance to lose to the Dodgers in October…" Well, it's October, and… only the Braves lost to the Dodgers therein. Every other team either lost to someone else, didn't make the postseason, or has their season still ongoing.

It's fitting, perhaps, that with the Dodgers eliminated, none of the remaining teams still "in it" have a payroll in baseball's top half. The Brewers are 20th (19th by luxury tax balance), the Guardians are dead last (29th), and the Rays are 28th (27th). So much for that narrative surviving the spin cycle that is MLB trying to shoehorn a short series playoff format onto this sport and league.

But, all of that doesn't mean you don't have feelings about the Dodgers bowing out. (Or, getting steamed out like a rug stain.) So, if you do, what are they?

articles.title: Packing a wallop
articles.summary: When you rush for 310 yards, it’s normally a good day. And Glacier had a great day as Trey Ramey ran wild and the Wolfpack downed Crosstown rival Flathead 51...
articles.body:
When you rush for 310 yards, it's normally a good day.

And Glacier had a great day as Trey Ramey ran wild and the Wolfpack downed Crosstown rival Flathead 51-7 in the 20th meeting of the two teams Thursday at Legends Stadium.

Ramey ran the ball 13 times for 237 yards, including a 79-yarder that was a shoestring tackle away from going the length of the field. He still scored two touchdowns on the ground.

The Wolfpack (7-1, 6-0 in Western AA games) also found a trio of passing scores, two to Liam Palmer and one to Cooper Pelc.

"(Palmer) is tough. He has courage," Glacier coach Grady Bennett said. "When you run the hurdles and you learn those things and you bring that to the football field, he is such a competitor. He has gotten more of a chance at wide receiver with Dylan (Banzet) being hurt, and he is really stepping up."

Palmer's 42-yard grab on the final play of the first half felt like an early dagger that put Glacier ahead 35-0.

"I got off the ball and shook the corner, then I had to go get it. It had to be my ball," Palmer said.

Flathead (3-5, 1-5) was without quarterback Bear Barker, who is battling an injury to his throwing shoulder. Leum Saisbury — who is normally a running back and just returned from missing two games with an injury — started at quarterback.

"I am really proud of our defense, and even our coaches. Knowing that he is the leading running back at the time in the backfield with another good running back, we could have gone to a four-down or five-down front and packed the box," Bennett said. "We could have packed the box, but we stayed with what we do and a three-down front and I think it is going to serve us well down the road."

"For us, not having our quarterback and having to institute a new offense in a couple of days, it's tough," Flathead coach Mac Roche said. "Hats off to them, they executed and played a good ball game."

Ramey started strong on Glacier's first offensive possession as he ripped off a 23-yard run before going 34 yards to score the game's first touchdown.

Next Wolfpack drive, it was Eli Imperato's turn as the senior doubled the advantage from 11 yards out to make it 14-0.

Palmer caught his first touchdown early in the second quarter, a 20-yard catch-and-run on the play after Ramey's 79-yard dash. Flathead had pinned Glacier at its 1-yard line on a punt.

Keim and Pelc connected with five minutes left in the first half to make it 28-0 with an 8-yard touchdown pass. Then Keim found Palmer on the deep post to cap off a dominant first half.

Ramey added his second rushing score of the game late in the third quarter, before the Glacier defense forced a safety to extend the lead to 44-0.

Kyle West then showed off his sprinter speed to go 21 yards and find Glacier's final touchdown of the game.

Flathead broke the shutout bid with two minutes left as Silus Marquart connected with Liam Rech from 5 yards away to make it 51-7.

Glacier heads on the road to close out the regular season with Missoula Big Sky (7-1, 5-1); the winner of that matchup will claim the Western AA title and No. 1 seed for the playoffs.

Flathead remains home to battle Missoula Sentinel, trying to close out their season on a high note. Both games kick off at 7 p.m.

articles.title: Friday Flakes: So Who Gets to Play Quarterback for Oregon on Saturday against Nebraska?
articles.summary: Oregon has three options to start at Quarterback against Nebraska. Which one gets the nod?
articles.body:
In case you have been living under a college football rock, Oregon will be without their starting quarterback Dante Moore on Saturday when Nebraska travels to Eugene, OR. Before the season Moore was picked by many to be the top quarterback to be selected in next year's draft but he was injured against USC.

This week Dan Lanning has said that it is an open competition to determine who will start against Nebraska.

Option 1 : Dylan Raiola, played extremely well against USC after the Moore injury. Then last week happened against UCLA. It is widely considered to be Raiola's worst game of his career as he threw for 43 yards on 6/19 passing with two interceptions.

Oregon fans were licking their chops watching Raiola go against Portland State and thought they had the next big thing. What Nebraska fans kept on saying is that he looked and continues to look a lot like he did when he played at Nebraska and that goes for the UCLA game as well.

Now could Oregon choose to start Raiola and then he goes out and beats Nebraska? Absolutely. That is right up Nebraska's alley.

Option 2 : Brock Thomas relieved Raiola after his disastrous start and actually played pretty well. He threw for 156 yards and a touchdown against UCLA. He didn't turn the ball over and that probably will work in his favor.

Option 3 : Akili Smith Jr. Dan Lanning had the following to say about Smith Jr.:

"Absolutely, and Akili's done a really good job and he's probably the one that's the most different from a from a package standpoint and things that you can carry and do different with Akili….But he has a really strong arm, been able to connect vertically on shots. Obviously, his feet become a weapon…And are a real tool for us as well. But yeah, he's done a really good job."

Now, Akili Smith has thrown only four passes all season and that was against Portland State.

The Verdict (or Prediction) : It is my prediction that Oregon will start Brock Thomas and use Akili Smith in certain packages throughout the game. Nebraska will not be able to prepare itself for what it has not seen on game film. Maybe he will be used in the redzone. I will be surprised if we see Dylan Raiola. I wonder if Dan Lanning wonders how well Dylan will be ready mentally after having such a disastrous game against UCLA and then going up against his former team. It would be an emotionally charged matchup for sure.

articles.title: Florida State at Miami preview: Breaking down the Seminoles
articles.summary: Florida State heads to Miami with a record-setting quarterback and plenty to prove after another difficult road loss.
articles.body:
Florida State football arrives at Hard Rock Stadium on Saturday, Oct 17, needing a more complete performance against the University of Miami Hurricanes, a team that has yet to lose this season. The Seminoles also look to snap an 11-game road losing streak.

FSU is coming off a 44-20 defeat at the University of Louisville after letting a 14-point first-quarter lead slip away. The No. 3 Miami enters the rivalry game following a bye week and a 41-13 victory over Clemson University.

"These are the games why you come to Florida State," offensive coordinator Tim Harris Jr. said in a press conference on Oct. 12. "These are the ones you think about."

For the 'Noles, the matchup is another chance to prove their best moments can last beyond the opening quarter.

"It's not a motivational issue," head coach Mike Norvell said in a press conference on Oct. 12. "It's handling the emotional swings that you see and they've shown the capability to do that really well."

Daniels presents a challenge beyond the pocket

Fifth-year quarterback Ashton Daniels has given the Garnet and Gold a different dimension with his mobility. Through six games, he has thrown for 1,320 yards and rushed for a conference-leading 10 touchdowns.

His biggest rushing performance came against the University of Virginia on Oct. 3, when he ran for 136 yards and five touchdowns, a program record for a quarterback, in a 38-7 victory. Florida State also benefited from a defense that registered 10 sacks and limited Virginia to 37 rushing yards.

Against Louisville, Daniels completed 21 of 37 passes for 209 yards and two touchdowns and added a rushing score. However, the Seminoles went scoreless in the second half, making an encouraging opening stretch feel distant by the final whistle.

Offensive supporting cast needs greater consistency Saturday

Sophomore running back Ousmane Kromah leads FSU on the ground with 565 rushing yards, second in the Atlantic Coast Conference. He has gained at least 80 yards in all six games, including 88 on 19 carries against Louisville.

The 'Noles have additional options through the air. Sophomore wide receiver Jayvan Boggs leads the team with 299 receiving yards, while sophomore wide receiver Micahi Danzy caught both of Daniels' touchdown passes at Louisville.

Senior wide receiver Duce Robinson, who led the Garnet and Gold with 1,081 receiving yards last season, remains another potential difference-maker.

"We need Duce Robinson to be a major impact for this team and I feel he is," Norvell said. "It's about being able to get him more opportunities as well as making sure we're capitalizing on all things as it plays out throughout the course of that game."

Explosive rushing plays expose ongoing defensive problems

Florida State showed its defensive potential against Virginia, holding the Cavaliers to seven points and 205 total yards. Six days later, the same unit gave up 397 rushing yards to Louisville.

Louisville junior running back Isaac Brown finished with 235 yards, including a 97-yard touchdown immediately after the Seminoles turned the ball over on downs at Louisville's 3-yard line. Instead of stretching a 14-0 lead, FSU allowed a big play that helped swing the game.

"It always starts with me," defensive coordinator Tony White said in a press conference on Oct. 12. "It takes one guy to be in the gap or get cut out and a 50-yard touchdown run. Some of that is situation in the game and some of that is playcalling."

The 'Noles will have to limit explosive plays and avoid giving Miami short fields to keep the game close into the second half. Norvell also stressed the need to improve the team's fundamentals against the run.

"We want to be a defense that sets the edge," Norvell said. "We're not doing that good enough."

Miami's passing attack adds another difficult matchup

The Garnet and Gold will also face junior quarterback Darian Mensah, who completed 18 of 27 passes for 227 yards in Miami's win at Clemson. The Hurricanes have shown the ability to score quickly, including a 61-yard touchdown pass on their first offensive play in that game.

"[Mensah] is tough to pressure, he's really good against the blitz," Norvell said. "He's good versus zone coverage, man coverage."

Florida State therefore faces a difficult balance: generating pressure on Mensah without surrendering another game-changing play. Miami also held Clemson to 55 rushing yards and recorded six sacks, creating another challenge for Daniels and Kromah.

The Seminoles enter the weekend with the weight of an 11-game road losing streak on their backs. Ending that streak against an undefeated rival would require the consistency that has been missing in recent losses.

Kickoff is scheduled for 7 p.m. Saturday at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens.

articles.title: Eric Bieniemy on heated sideline discussion with Patrick Mahomes
articles.summary: During Thursday's press conference, Kansas City Chiefs OC Eric Bieniemy reflected on a heated sideline discussion with Patrick Mahomes | @EdEastonJr
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy spoke with reporters on Thursday. He reflected on a heated sideline conversation with Patrick Mahomes during the Week 4 win over the Las Vegas Raiders.

"I have no problems with guys venting their frustrations, because I want them to; that's part of the dynamics of the relationships that we have," said Bieniemy. "Sometimes you're going to agree with things, sometimes you're going to disagree with things. If there's something that's taking place out on the field, they might have a better view than what we do off the field."

Television cameras caught Mahomes and Bieniemy in an animated sideline discussion. The two-time league MVP seemed frustrated, but Bieniemy embraced the public reaction.

"I want them to be comfortable sharing that stuff with me. There are no issues of communications. We're in the arena. It's all about survival. Sometimes you get their best, and sometimes you get their worst," said Bieniemy. "I'm inviting all of that, because I'd rather hear him (Mahomes) air his frustrations at me than to vent it in a different place where it's not going to be taken the right way."

Bieniemy has had fiery conversations with players in past seasons, and Travis Kelce has often expressed his feelings toward head coach Andy Reid publicly during games.

"There's so many things that take course throughout the course of a game," Bieniemy said. "I probably cussed someone out about something, but that stuff, it happens. Not that you ever take anything personally. Like I said, sometimes there's agreements and disagreements. Throughout the course of a game, things happen."

Mahomes has recorded 1,037 passing yards, 9 passing touchdowns, and 2 interceptions through 4 games this season.

Liverpool are conducting late fitness checks on Alexander Isak , Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai ahead of Saturday's Premier League clash with Brentford .

Giovanni Leoni remains out with an ACL injury but could return to training during the next international break.

Ryan Gravenberch will also miss Brentford through suspension after his red card against Manchester City. He is available again against Brighton on October 25.

articles.title: Heat’s Davion Mitchell making clear he won’t stay down or slow down
articles.summary: If Davion Mitchell had something to prove to the Miami Heat this preseason, that mission was accomplished even before Friday night’s exhibition finale agains...
articles.body:
If Davion Mitchell had something to prove to the Miami Heat this preseason, that mission was accomplished even before Friday night's exhibition finale against the Orlando Magic at Kia Center.

The Heat this season will operate at his speed.

The player listed as shortest on the roster arguably has stood tallest this preseason in multiple regards.

Toughness? That would be taking six stitches above his right eye and refusing to call it a night in Wednesday night's exhibition victory over the visiting Brooklyn Nets.

Leadership? That would be leaving anyone alongside in his dust if they can't keep up.

Tackling that latter element first, Giannis Antetokounmpo arguably still is attempting to catch his breath from all this Mitchell motoring this preseason.

"He's incredible. And he's tough to keep up with. He goes so fast," Antetokounmpo said of the pace that coach Erik Spoelstra again is encouraging.

"I love playing with him. He always makes the right play. No matter if they score or don't score, we get the rebound, we're going the other way."

Because Mitchell won't stand for standing around.

"I mean, because that's the way we play," Mitchell said, with the Heat next off for four days before Wednesday's season opener against the Minnesota Timberwolves at Kaseya Center. "And I know I can get in the paint anytime I want. And if I can get just a one on one, for the most part I'm getting the paint. And I'm going to make the right play.

"I'm going to pass it the majority of the time. So I just try to, I just try to get in the paint when the defense is not ready. That's kind of just my goal."

All while wisely keeping a watchful eye on Antetokounmpo .

"He's always going to make the right pass for myself," the Heat's prized offseason acquisition said. "Whenever I feel like I haven't touched the ball in two or three possessions, he's always going to check in with me and make sure I get a touch and be able to open it from the post or from the wing. It's fun playing with him."

Mitchell also has proven more than willing to share the wealth.

"I think that if we get the rebound, we can score anytime we get the rebound because we're one of the fastest teams and we've got a lot of players who can make plays," he said.

Which is why Mitchell wants to be out there, be a part of it, dictating the pace.

So that meant a quick turnaround Wednesday night from taking six stitches above his right eye early in the third quarter, getting patched up, and playing on.

"I just love the game," the 6-foot, 200-pound guard said. "And I just wanted to play. I just wanted to be out there. You kind of don't take these moments for granted. And I know if I can play, I'm gonna go out there and play.

"So it wasn't really a hard decision for me. After they told me I got to shoot the free throws to stay in the game, I just ran out there and shot them."

Then he got patched up, conducting his postgame media session with a significant bandage above the eye.

"As he was going off," Spoelstra said of their interaction in the huddle following Mitchell's collision with Nets guard Keon Ellis, "he was like, 'This is just going to be a handful of stitches. I want to play. I want to get my minutes like everybody else was able to do' and we allowed him to do that. He still wanted to play in the fourth quarter.

"He loves the game. He loves competing. He wants to get out there and compete in the games, not just the practices. So I get it."

articles.title: Everything Texans QB C.J. Stroud said on Marvin Harrison Jr. joning franchise
articles.summary: Here's everything Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud had to say before the team's road trip to London for a Week 6 matchup against the Jacksonville Jagua...
articles.body:
Here's everything Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud had to say before the team's road trip to London for a Week 6 matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars , including his thoughts on the reunion with Marvin Harrison Jr., his role in the offense and more.

Question: On reconnecting with WR Marvin Harrison Jr.

C.J. Stroud: "I'm happy to have 'Marv'. Everybody's been saying how much of a good dude he is, how nice he's been. It's nice to have my guy back and I'm excited to be rolling with him."

Q: On first meeting WR Marvin Harrison Jr.

Stroud: "His freshman year, my sophomore year, that was my first year starting. He really didn't play much, but he always showed up in practice. Most people probably remember him from the Rose Bowl. I think he had three touchdowns and 100-some yards, but Jaxon [Smith-Njigba] had a great game as well. I've always known he was special when he came in, he was super ahead of his game, just really mature. Him and Emeka [Egbuka] were some of the most mature freshmen that I've been around and then just his work ethic and it's the same thing now. Those are kind of some of the memories that I have."

On WR Marvin Harrison Jr.'s strengths as a receiver

Stroud: "I would just say his route running. He's really good at running great routes. He gets open on time, I think he's a very quarterback-friendly receiver. The better you are with getting the ball at your hands on time, the better he is. I think that's why him and I had so much success because I'm a pocket quarterback that likes to throw it to him on time. That's when he's at his best. That's one of the great things he does."

Q: On WR Marvin Harrison Jr. fitting into the Texans ' culture

Stroud: "He'll fit in fine. He's all about what we believe in this organization and be great for us."

Q: On helping get WR Marvin Harrison Jr. up to speed

Stroud: "He has to learn it and he's a really smart kid. He's somebody who I'm not worried about. At the end of the day it's football. You run some very similar routes, just different ways. I'm very vocal on how I like things done. He knows that. We've had a conversations, we'll continue to just get on the same page, but a lot of the things are similar from where he's coming from. I think just the way I talk to him I think it helps."

Q: On preparing for the London game in Week 6

Stroud: "It's really just nutrition. Making sure I'm drinking enough fluids to keep my body hydrated and just sleeping on the right time zones and just adjust that way. I'm trying my best to be ready for when we go there and you have to play a game. I'm trying my best to just try new things and be adjusted."

Q: On the plan for the plane ride to London

Stroud: "Whatever they ask me to do. I think they're asking us to sleep as much as we can. I'll probably just sleep."

Q: On whether he helped push to trade for WR Marvin Harrison Jr.

Stroud: "I just asked for them to include me in things like that since I got here. I was just appreciative that they gave me an opportunity to even explain who I thought he was, the player I thought he was. I really don't have like that type of push or say so. I try to do my job and leave it up to our front office to make those decisions. I'm very happy he's here."

Q: On being a resource for WR Marvin Harrison Jr.

Stroud: "I don't think anybody ever is a finished product. You're always learning ways to get better. You're always learning ways to get better at what you're already good at. I think there are two different types of perspectives you can look from. You can look from the world's perspective of who people think you are or yourself. I think that's where I've learned that it doesn't really matter what people say. They can't really stop or start what you have going on. Then you have your perspective of who you think you are, who you believe you can be. I think that's more important. For Marvin he knows that. He's a heck of a player. I don't agree with some of the things that are being said about him. At the end of the day, that's what people who are on the outside are saying. I'm a firm believer of really focus on what you can control and then whatever other people say or have their opinions, kudos to them. They have platforms and things that they can say on, but that doesn't really affect you unless you make it. I think he'll be fine. I try to just be [a resource] to him if I need to. He's a confident dude. He'll be fine."

Stroud: "It's taken time. I'm still working on it now. I remember my rookie year, I was playing really well and everybody was gassing me up. I remember a time in college where everybody was really hard on me and really critical and then I kind of flipped the script and I started playing really well and everybody started loving me. I was like, 'Man, that's like kind of like weird.' People were just up and down. That was like the first time I've dealt with it. Then my rookie season, having like a great year, I forget who we played, but I had a really good game and I was up here and somebody asked me a question and I was like, 'I can't fall in love with the cheers or the boos, you have to stay very even keel.' And then last year, same thing for me. At the end of the day, people are going to have their opinion. They're going to have their critiques and rightfully so, people get paid a lot of money to judge people on what they're doing and we're in the entertainment business. We're not fined to not be critiqued. It's up to you to let that affect you or not. Every year is different. I grow, I can't say like I've arrived more than I was or it's just a different year, I'm a different human, I'm a different person. I make different decisions, I'm just different and I'll just try my best to let what I control be my mindset."

Stroud: "Very talented group. Somebody I've had a lot of history with. They've done a great job. Like you said, stopping the run. Josh Hines-Allen [Arik] Armstead and [Travon] Walker. I think they're great players. I think No. 23 [Foyesade Oluokoun], one of the best linebackers, very underrated. Then in the back end, they've been playing well as well. Really keeping a lot of teams to less points and I think they do a good job and changing up a lot of blitzes and things like that. I think they're a great group and we have to be prepared."

Q: On what excites him about the London trip

Stroud: "I would just say just playing in front of a different fan base. I think it's cool. I'm very grateful and appreciative to have this opportunity to play every week in the NFL, to even practice. I try not to take anything for granted. Having an opportunity to like play this game internationally, it's just dope to me. I'm excited to just go out there and see a different atmosphere. It might be very exciting or underwhelming. It's just kind of cool to like have like a little bit of a unknowingness to the environment we're playing in. It's a great team and a great opponent. I think it's going to be fun."

Stroud: "He brings explosiveness. He brings a grit. He's a very tough individual. Been through a lot in his life, also in his career. He's a home run hitter.
