articles.title: Eagles need more than Tanner McKee to end skid against Panthers
articles.summary: Jalen Hurts' absence headlines the story, but the Eagles face other challenges beyond the X's and O's against the Panthers in Week 6.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles are facing another difficult week, and recent developments have made their game against the Carolina Panthers even more complicated. Jalen Hurts has been ruled out of Sunday's game after the team announced that he is dealing with a superficial blood clot . Philadelphia has also said it is determining the appropriate course of treatment, emphasizing, as it should, that its franchise quarterback's health and safety are the utmost priority.

Everyone hopes Hurts makes a full recovery, but his absence creates an immediate football problem for a team already searching for answers. The Eagles have lost three consecutive games, and now Tanner McKee is expected to take over at quarterback in Week 6. He has two career starts and has completed 54 of 88 passes for 597 yards, five touchdowns, and one interception.

However, replacing Hurts in the middle of a difficult stretch presents a significant challenge. His medical emergency understandably dominates the conversation, but it isn't the only factor that could shape Sunday's outcome. Here are a few factors that will determine Week 6's outcome. Each issue tests a team that needs to stop its slide in a different way.

Can the Eagles shake off the London hangover against a Panthers team exiting a bye week?

Returning from an international game can disrupt sleep patterns and routines, forcing players and coaches to adjust after crossing several time zones. Philadelphia has had time to readjust since returning from London, but the Eagles have another concern heading into their game against Carolina: rest.

They have had just seven days between games, while the Panthers enter Week 6 with more rest. They haven't played since October 4th. The travel adjustment may be behind them, but the less-discussed rest disparity could still influence Sunday's matchup.

Can Nick Sirianni steady the locker room?

The Eagles have seen significant leadership changes, with Cam Jurgens gone and Lane Johnson retired. Jordan Mailata, Zack Baun, Jake Elliott, and others remain, but the personnel changes, consecutive losses, and Hurts' unexpected absence create an unfamiliar situation for the team.

This is where Sirianni's leadership matters most. His ability to keep the locker room focused and maintain belief in the team's direction could matter as much as any tactical adjustment. With McKee preparing to start, Philadelphia needs clarity from its coaching staff and confidence from the players around him. A strong response would let Sirianni show he can guide the team through adversity, something that has long been one of his calling cards.

Jake Elliott has had a productive start to the season, and Braden Mann has been one of Philadelphia's more consistent performers. However, the special teams unit enters this matchup with questions after a costly kickoff decision helped fuel the loss to Jacksonville in London .

The Eagles must avoid allowing that mistake to influence their next decisions. Special teams can change field position and scoring opportunities in seconds, so disciplined execution will be essential. Philadelphia needs to make sound decisions, avoid costly penalties, and trust its preparation rather than play cautiously out of fear of repeating the previous week's mistake.

The Eagles have more than one problem to solve against Carolina, and Hurts' absence makes the margin for error even smaller. McKee's performance will draw attention, but the team's response will depend on more than the quarterback position. If Philadelphia handles the travel, finds leadership in a changing locker room, and executes cleanly on special teams, it will give itself a better chance to end its losing streak.

articles.title: ‘It’s done’: Michael Carrick outlines Lisandro Martinez stance after explosive Man United criticism
articles.summary: Martinez criticised United’s technical director Jason Wilcox for not doing enough to strengthen Carrick’s squad following Tuesday’s defeat at Atletico Madrid
articles.body:
Michael Carrick said he accepted Lisandro Martinez 's apology for his explosive criticisms of Manchester United and director of football Jason Wilcox this week and believes his team can be galvanised by the row.

The United manager said he will carry on picking the Argentinian defender and feels that, far from being distracted, his team could benefit from it.

And Carrick insisted the harmony in the squad has not been disrupted by Martinez complaining about a lack of buys and implying he was not happy with the signings Wilcox did oversee in the summer.

While Martinez, in a statement he released on Thursday, did not retract some of his comments about Wilcox, he held talks with Carrick and the United hierarchy.

And Carrick said: "He's released his statement, and he's realised he's made a mistake, and I think that's enough for all of us to move on with. The acknowledgement of what's been done has certainly been enough, and we've moved on, and we're definitely not looking back at it now."

Carrick confirmed the defender is available for selection for Sunday's trip to Leeds. "He is part of the squad, yeah," said the United manager.

United have only won two of their first nine games in all competitions this season but Carrick feels they can emerge stronger from a trying week.

He added: "There's a real sense and a feeling within the group that we want to do something about this situation, and we want to do something about it really quickly. You understand the situation that came up after the game, but it's been dealt with, and we have moved on, genuinely moved on.

"The squad today was in a fantastic place, better than I've seen it for a while and that's it, plain and simple. We're emotional, we're passionate, we care a lot. Sometimes someone says something that's a little bit maybe shouldn't say it at a certain time, but that doesn't distract us from what we're creating here and the environment and the spirit within the group. It's not affected.

"Certain situations, it can galvanise the group, and it's certainly galvanised the group as this week's progressed, and the boys are in a really good place right now."

United are waiting to see if left-back Luke Shaw and midfielder Kobbie Mainoo are fit enough to return at Leeds.

articles.title: 5 Tarik Skubal landing spots (Mets?) as free agency begins for Dodgers ace
articles.summary: Who could end up signing two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal? The Mets? The Yankees?
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are officially out of the 2026 MLB playoffs after an NLCS sweep at the hands of the Milwaukee Brewers , and that means the clock has started on Tarik Skubal's free agency.

The two-time Cy Young winner was dealt to the Dodgers mid-season and finished with a 2.36 ERA in 10 regular-season games, and with a labor dispute looming, things could get complicated even if he's the biggest name by far on the market. Still, it's worth asking: Where will the soon-to-be 30-year-old ace sign?

Let's dive in with five teams who could be possible landing spots as the bidding begins, in no particular order:

The obvious answer. He re-signs in L.A. for a ton of money -- maybe some of it deferred -- and the Dodgers keep one of the best pitchers in baseball. It wouldn't be that surprising given that they traded for him in the first place.

Now we get into the list of teams that can afford a player like Skubal (but hey, if there's a salary cap! We won't assume anything about that just yet). The Mets and their deep-pocketed owner would be happy to make a splash and secure a front-line starter, something New York needs going into next season.

Cam Schlittler, Max Fried, Gerrit Cole, Carlos Rodon... and Skubal? That would be downright nasty. There might be questions about the Yankees' lineup heading into this offseason, but a signing like that will silence some of the overall questions.

They could use an ace and we've seen Toronto be in the mix for big-name free agents before. This wouldn't be too crazy of a landing spot for Skubal.

Garrett Crochet is awesome, but beyond that, the Red Sox could use some front-line starter help. Does the franchise take out the checkbook here?

articles.summary: Rory McIlroy was one of a number of players impacted after the second round of the DP World India Championship was suspended due to fading light.
articles.body:
DP World India Championship, day two leaderboard

8 J Luiten (Ned), A Hidalgo (Spa), AMeronk (Pol), T Detry (Bel) (7*); -7 E Pepperell (Eng), T Clements (Eng), E Lopez-Chacarra (Spa) (5*)

*Denotes number of holes played before play ended on day one

Rory McIlroy was one of a number of players impacted after the second round of the DP World India Championship was suspended due to fading light.

England's Eddie Pepperell and Todd Clements are both one shot off the four-way tie for the lead as they completed their 18 holes in New Dehli.

Joost Luiten, Angel Hidalgo and Adrian Meronk all finished their rounds and lead on eight under par, while Belgium's Thomas Detry is also tied at the top despite having his round cut short after seven holes.

Northern Ireland's Tom McKibbin started the second round one shot off the lead but had fallen to three back, on five-under par, after seven holes.

Five-time major winner McIlroy is tied for 17th on four-under but his challenge was halted after four holes.

The Northern Ireland player started his second round with a superb eagle and had shot three pars before the hooter sounded to end play.

England's Tommy Fleetwood and Scotland's Robert MacIntyre were also hit by the end of play after the fourth hole, and join McIlroy on four-under par and four shots off the leaders.

The delays come after heavy rain and thunderstorms led to play being suspended for five hours in Thursday's opening round, and the second round will resume at 02:45 BST on Saturday.
